articles.title: Six of Veritasium's Last 51 Videos Changed Title Between My Reads. MKBHD's Changed None
articles.excerpt: I run a visa agency in Bali, and in the evenings I build scrapers on Apify. One of them lists the videos of a YouTube channel: YouTube Channel Videos Scraper. You give it handles, it reads the Videos,…
articles.body: I run a visa agency in Bali, and in the evenings I build scrapers on Apify. One of them lists the videos of a YouTube channel: YouTube Channel Videos Scraper . You give it handles, it reads the Videos, Shorts or Live tab the way the website does and returns one row per video. I check it with the same small job every few days: the latest 50 videos of @veritasium and @mkbhd . Same input, same tab, nothing clever. Between 14 and 22 November that job ran ten times, and I kept the datasets. When I put them side by side I expected the view counts to move. I didn't expect the titles to. The job { "channels" : [ "veritasium" , "mkbhd" ] , "tab" : "videos" , "maxVideosPerChannel" : 50 } Every one of the ten runs returned 100 rows, 50 per channel.
articles.author: Matvey

articles.title: How to turn a weekly status report into a 5-slide deck
articles.excerpt: A weekly status report fails when it tries to be a diary. The room does not need every task you touched. It needs enough context to decide what happens next. If people leave still asking "so what do y…
articles.body: A weekly status report fails when it tries to be a diary. The room does not need every task you touched. It needs enough context to decide what happens next. If people leave still asking "so what do you need from us?", the file did not do its job. Before you open a new deck, write the week down in four lines: what changed, why it matters, what you recommend, and what is still open. Those four lines are the deck. Everything else is backup. Use the same five-slide skeleton every week. The numbers move; the structure does not. That is what lets a returning audience skim. People who already trust the format can find the ask in the first ten seconds. Slide 1: the week in one page Put the date range in the title, not in a subtitle people will miss.
articles.author: slide-deck.io

articles.title: GitHub Actions Accepts Invalid YAML. actionlint and yamllint Don't Catch It
articles.excerpt: GitHub Actions will run a workflow file that isn't valid YAML. The bug comes down to one missing space in a multi-line single-quoted string, and it's in a real, public repo's workflow where GitHub sti…
articles.body: GitHub Actions will run a workflow file that isn't valid YAML. The bug comes down to one missing space in a multi-line single-quoted string, and it's in a real, public repo's workflow where GitHub still runs that step without an error. I ran actionlint 1.7.12 and yamllint 1.38.0 on it and neither one complained. zizmor refuses to parse it, and for over a year zizmor has been the one taking the blame. William Woodruff, who maintains zizmor , wrote it up on 2026-11-22 in a TIL called "GitHub Actions accepts invalid YAML" . I read the post, the zizmor issue behind it and the runner source, then ran the examples through the linters most of us have in pre-commit. At the end there's the lint setup I'd use to match what GitHub actually enforces.
articles.author: Alan West

articles.body: The best-known AI coding tool isn't the top-ranked one on the board I run. GitHub Copilot, probably the most familiar name in AI coding, scores 7.40 out of 10 overall this morning. Cursor leads the coding agents category at 8.45, with Claude Code at 8.40 and Windsurf at 8.05. Copilot sits fourth of six. That gap is worth a minute of any owner's time, because most AI tool purchases get made on one of two shortcuts: buy the cheapest option, or buy the name everyone has heard of. Neither one is the same as buying the best value. Why the big name feels safe A familiar brand lowers the perceived risk of a purchase. Your team has heard of it, IT may already approve it, and nobody gets blamed for picking the market leader. Copilot earns a lot of that trust honestly.

articles.excerpt: The Cairn AI framework is proving to be a boon for defenders and attackers.
articles.body: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.

November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

articles.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
articles.excerpt: Researchers have successfully grown potatoes in simulated lunar regolith, possibly opening the door for farming on future moon bases.
articles.body: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.

articles.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
articles.excerpt: How realistic are the zero-g sports we see in sci-fi? We talk to Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, to find out.
articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game.
